slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you
quietly impressive
Finishing what you start. The book, the course, the side project. Most people abandon things halfway. The guy who quietly finishes is the one people end up respecting.
Knowing one skill really well. Cooking, fixing bikes, drawing, a language. Deep skill in one thing earns a calm kind of respect that no amount of talking ever can.
Being early without mentioning it. You arrive, you're ready, you say nothing about it. People notice reliability long before they notice anything you say about yourself.
Knowing a bit about everything. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I can join almost any conversation with something interesting to add.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I can join almost any conversation with something interesting to add.

slides.texte_overlay: Staying humble about your wins. Got promoted, ran a marathon, learned an instrument? Let others find out. Quiet achievements impress far more than loud announcements.
Treating waiters and strangers with real respect. How you speak to people who can do nothing for you shows your character better than any first impression ever will.
Keeping your body strong. Training three times a week, without posting about it. Strength you never show off makes you look disciplined, healthy and steady.
